flags.note: 'Hardly unreserved' is understatement for a review that is mostly negative; the double negative plus four 'un-' options makes it a decoding task. Reads fine, but 'hardly unreserved' fits a mostly positive review with some reservations better than a mostly negative one.

S047-01.notes: Admiring one element while faulting most others means the verdict had reservations. A (uninformed) has no support, and nothing suggests the review was unrequested (B). D (unoriginal) is a plausible trap, since 'hardly unoriginal' could be read as praise, but the colon's evidence concerns mixed judgment, not originality.

flags.note: The design has no marigold-free control, so it isolates fungi only. A is limited to 'does not depend on soil fungi', which is properly hedged.

S047-02.notes: Killing the fungi did not change the result, so the fungus explanation is undercut. D would need pots without marigolds, which the study did not have. B and C are not tested.

S047-03.notes: The conclusion is about relative benefit, so it needs the difference between users and nonusers within each group (8 vs 4). A is the strongest trap: it gives a raw gain without the nonuser baseline. B covers one group only, and C does not compare the groups' benefits.

S047-04.notes: Vint holds TV exposure constant and finds dialect use varies with face-to-face contact. A contradicts her claim that broadcast speech is not the cause. C: she does not dispute the change. D has no support.

flags.note: Inference rests on the analogy to 'letters she did not intend to answer'; one might also read pride or a suspicion that the book does not exist, but C remains the only supportable option.

S047-05.notes: Putting the slip in the drawer of letters she will not answer signals she will not follow through. She wrote the title down, so B is wrong. D reverses the meaning, and nothing mentions suppliers (A).

S047-06.notes: Rail towns adopting standard time earlier ties the change to railroads. A shows the railroads needed schedules but not that they ended sun time. C and D are off target.

S047-07.notes: The opening dash needs a closing dash: 'founders—two retired teachers, a baker, and a local historian—never expected'. A comma (A) mismatches the dash, a semicolon (B) cuts off the subject from its verb, and C leaves the appositive unclosed.

S047-08.notes: The plural subject 'notebooks' needs a finite verb. B, C and D leave the sentence without a main verb, making it a fragment.

S047-09.notes: He built a mirror telescope as a result of believing lenses could not be fixed. 'Nevertheless' is tempting because of 'wrongly', but his action follows from his conclusion, not against it. C and D do not fit.

S047-10.notes: Only C gives the finding (4 vs 11) together with the limitation (SO2 not measured, so there are alternative causes). A overclaims cause, B leaves out both the finding and the limitation, and D leaves out the finding.
